entry.name: preset
entry.description: preset can store and recall the parameters of any specified user interface objects at the click of a mouse. It can also be used as a user interface link to a named pattrstorage object.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Clicking on a button in theobject will recall a stored preset.Shift-clicking on a button in theobject will store a preset.The number of visible presets can be adjusted by resizing theobject's box. The maximum number of presets in a singleobject is 2048.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: If a preset with a matching name is found, it is recalled.

messages.name: bang
messages.description: Sends out the settings of the preset that was most recently recalled with anor a mouse click.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: Erases the contents of the most recently sent preset. The word, followed by a number, erases the contents of that numbered preset.

messages.name: clearall
messages.description: Erases the contents of all presets.

messages.name: float
messages.description: A float recalls a preset that is a linear interpolation between two adjacent presets. The first preset is the integer part of the float value and the second preset is the next highest integer. The weight of the first preset is 1 minus the decimal part of the float value. The weight of the second preset is the decimal part of the float value. For example with an input of 2.7, preset 2 will contribute 30% and preset 3 will contribute 70%. Not all objects that store data in a preset can interpolate their stored data. For these objects, the data used will be selected from the preset slot with the highest weighting.

messages.name: int
messages.description: Sending any integer will trigger the preset of the same number.

messages.name: name
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sets the ID Name for the preset. The ID Name allows the preset to have a unique ID so that files created for it will not read into other presets.

messages.name: read
messages.description: The word, followed by no arguments or a number, displays an Open Document dialog box for choosing a file of preset data to read. If the preset has been given a Preset Name Code, only files of the type specified by the code will be displayed. The number argument specifies the preset number into which the file data should be read. If the number is 0 or -1, the data in the file will be read into the number of presets contained in the file starting with the first one. If the wordis followed by a symbol or a number and a symbol, no dialog box is displayed. Instead, the symbol is taken as a filename from which to read presets. The number functions as previously described.

messages.name: recallmulti
messages.description: The arguments toare a series of float values representing preset slots (the integer part) and weights (the decimal part). The preset values recalled are the weighted combination of all the presets. Weights are normalized so they are not required to add to 1. Example:will combine preset slots 4, 6, and 3 with weights of 0.6, 0.1, and 0.3 respectively. Not all objects that store data in a preset can interpolate their stored data. For these objects, the data used will be selected from the preset slot with the highest weighting.

messages.name: setname
messages.description: followed by anslot number and a name, assigns the name to the slot number. Names will be displayed when moving the mouse over a slot or when connecting aorobject to a. Once assigned a name, presets can be recalled by sending the name as a message.If the slot number is 0, the name will be assigned to the current preset.

messages.name: store
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, stores the current setting of all user interface objects in the same window in the preset indicated by the number. If an optional name argument is present, it is assigned to the stored preset.Presets are numbered left-to-right, top-to-bottom. When settings are stored in a preset, the dot's color changes to indicate that it contains something. Settings can also be stored in a preset by holding down the Shift key and clicking on the preset with the mouse.

messages.name: write
messages.description: The word, followed by no arguments or a number, displays a Save As dialog box for specifying a destination filename for writing the preset data. If the preset has been given a Preset Name Code, the file is given this code as its file type. The number argument specifies the preset number from which the preset data should be written. If the number is 0 or -1, all presets will be written. If the wordis followed by a symbol or a number and a symbol, no dialog box is displayed. Instead, the symbol is taken as a filename to use for writing the data, and the file will be placed in the current default folder. The number functions as previously described.
